title: Personal Credit Cards: Credit Limit Ranges and Over-Limit Tolerance
content:
Each tier of Personal Credit Cards is issued within a fixed band of credit limits, and each tier allows purchases to be authorized a stated percentage beyond the limit. No Personal Credit Cards tier ever bills an over-limit fee.

| Tier | Lowest credit limit issued | Highest credit limit the card may carry | Authorization tolerance above the limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | 300.00 USD | 5000.00 USD | 0 percent |
| College Rewards Visa | 500.00 USD | 3000.00 USD | 0 percent |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 1000.00 USD | 25000.00 USD | 5 percent |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 1000.00 USD | 25000.00 USD | 5 percent |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 5000.00 USD | 50000.00 USD | 10 percent |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 15000.00 USD | 100000.00 USD | 10 percent |

## Reading the tolerance

The tolerance is a percentage of the credit limit by which the balance may stand above that limit after a purchase is authorized. A tolerance of 0 percent means a purchase is authorized only while the balance after it stays within the limit itself.

> Worked example with hypothetical figures: on a Travel Rewards Visa Signature account with a limit of 8000.00 USD, the tolerance is 10 percent of 8000.00 USD, which is 800.00 USD, so purchases can be authorized while the balance after the purchase is no higher than 8800.00 USD. On a College Rewards Visa account with a limit of 1200.00 USD, the ceiling is the limit of 1200.00 USD itself.

## Basis Q&A

- **Can a limit fall outside its tier's band?** An approved limit sits between the lowest and highest figures shown for the tier.
- **Is a fee charged when the tolerance is used?** No; the tolerance never triggers an over-limit fee on any tier.
